description: CoveredEntity;BusinessAssociate

Six categories a covered entity may use/disclose PHI without authorization: (1) to the individual; (2) treatment, payment, health care operations; (3) opportunity to agree or object; (4) incident to a permitted use; (5) public interest and benefit activities; (6) limited data set
Use/disclosure required by law including statute, regulation, or court orders

Disclosures to public health authorities for disease/injury prevention and control, FDA-regulated product safety, communicable disease exposure notification, and work-related illness/injury surveillance to employers
Disclosures to appropriate government authorities regarding victims of abuse, neglect, or domestic violence
Disclosures to health oversight agencies for audits and investigations overseeing the health care system and government benefit programs
Disclosures in a judicial or administrative proceeding via court/tribunal order, or via subpoena with satisfactory assurances or a protective order

Disclosures to law enforcement officials under six specified circumstances and subject to conditions (e.g. as required by law, to identify/locate a suspect, about a victim, to report a death, evidence of a crime on premises, medical emergency)
Disclosures to funeral directors and to coroners or medical examiners to identify a deceased person, determine cause of death, and other authorized functions
Use/disclosure to facilitate donation and transplantation of cadaveric organs, eyes, and tissue
Use/disclosure for research with IRB/Privacy Board waiver, preparatory-to-research or decedent representations, or via a limited data set with a data use agreement
Disclosures believed necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to a person or the public, made to someone able to prevent/lessen the threat
Disclosures for essential government functions: military mission, national security/intelligence, protective services, correctional institutions, and government benefit program eligibility/enrollment
Disclosures as authorized by and to comply with workers' compensation and similar work-related injury/illness benefit laws
Written, plain-language authorization required for uses/disclosures not otherwise permitted or required (e.g. to a life insurer, employer, or for marketing); includes right to revoke

Marketing communications require individual authorization, with defined exceptions (face-to-face communications, nominal promotional gifts, and certain health-related communications); remuneration must be disclosed

Covered entity must limit use, disclosure, and requests of PHI to the minimum necessary; not required for treatment disclosures, disclosures to the individual, authorized disclosures, to HHS, or as required by law
Individual right to review and obtain a copy of their PHI in a designated record set, subject to specified exceptions and cost-based fees
Individual right to have a covered entity amend inaccurate or incomplete PHI in a designated record set
Individual right to an accounting of certain disclosures of their PHI for up to the six years preceding the request
Individual right to request restrictions on use/disclosure of PHI; covered entity is not obligated to agree but must honor agreed restrictions except in a medical emergency
Individual right to request receipt of communications by alternative means or at alternative locations
Individual right to, and covered entity duty to provide, a notice of privacy practices describing uses/disclosures, individual rights, entity duties, and complaint contact
Contrary State laws are preempted by the Privacy Rule unless the State law is more stringent/provides greater privacy protection or qualifies for a specified exception determined by HHS
